findings.title: Noul does not say what yes and no mean
findings.message: The question carries no criteria, so where the line between yes and no falls is left to the model.
findings.hint: The instruction is enough for many Nouls. Where the boundary is subtle, saying what a yes and a no mean is what moves a question from guessing to deciding.
findings.suggest: Add a `criteria` object with a `true` and a `false` description, saying which material counts as each.

findings.title: Another primitive fits these answers better
findings.message: The answer this asks for is not a noul, a choice or a score, but it is declared a `noul`.
findings.hint: Where two types both fit, prefer the one your code can act on directly. A Noul at 0.5 means yes and no are equally likely, not that the answer is in the middle. Accept it where the primitive is chosen for the caller rather than the question: a Noul whose probability you threshold, where a Choice would give you a label you would only threshold anyway.
findings.suggest: Change `type` to the primitive named, and reshape `criteria` to match it: a map of label to description for a Choice, an ordered list of described levels for a Score, a `true` and `false` pair for a Noul. Where no primitive is named, the answer is a value to be read out of the material rather than a judgement about it, so take the question out and read the value in code.

findings.title: The state holds a case the question does not settle
findings.message: The material holds a case on the edge of what this question asks, and nothing says which side it falls on.
findings.hint: A question is written against the material its author had in mind, and meets the material that arrives. "Does the text contain hello?" reads 0.59 against a state of "not hello", and 0.95 once the criteria say a negated mention still counts, so the defect has a measured cost. The trigger is 0.45 because on twelve paragraphs with an edge planted in them, run twice, the arms that should fire read 0.48 and up and the arms that should not read 0.32 and down. This is advice and not a warning because its rate on clean material is not established: it fires on 5 of the 18 documentation questions that carry a state, the highest rate in this catalogue, and the case for those being real findings instead of false ones is one person reading five queries. Accept it where the edge case is settled by a convention the reader already shares, so naming it in the question would repeat what the material settles.
findings.suggest: Name the edge case and say where it belongs, in the instructions or in a criterion. Saying that a negated mention still counts as a mention moved a reading from 0.59 to 0.95 on the same state.
findings.advice_caveat: Read this one before acting on it. The rewrite it asks for is measured on one question; how often it points at a query that is already fine is not.
findings.evidence: Read: "The state reports an ECE of 0.113 for the noul bank."
findings.readings_of: one reading and a re-ask on the trigger

findings.title: Choice has no fallback option
findings.message: None of the options is an `other` or `none of the above`.
findings.hint: Without a catch-all the probability mass has nowhere to go, so it lands on the nearest wrong label. Measured on decision-v7: where the answer was none of the options, removing the catch-all put a mean 0.79 on a label that could not be right and cost a Brier score of 0.660 against 0.349 with it. Where the answer was among the options it cost nothing.
findings.suggest: Add `"other": "Anything the other options do not cover"`.

value.other: Anything the other options do not cover

findings.title: State is large
findings.message: The state is large enough that unrelated detail is likely to be costing accuracy.
findings.hint: Retrieve and filter in code first, and send only the fields the questions need. This rule counts characters, which is a proxy for tokens, not a measurement of them.
findings.suggest: Build the state from the fields the questions read, and leave the rest out.
